title: Complexity bound of ceil-log of range and codomain sizes
statement:
Let $X$ be an arbitrary type and let $Y$ and $\alpha$ be finite nonempty types. Then for every function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, the deterministic communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
\[
  D(f) \;\le\; \lceil \log_2 \abs{Y} \rceil + \lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha} \rceil,
\]
where $\abs{Y}$ and $\abs{\alpha}$ denote the cardinalities of $Y$ and $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is an arbitrary two-argument function
replaced:
For finite, nonempty types $Y$ and $\alpha$ and any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$,
the deterministic communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}(f) \;\le\; \lceil\log_2 |Y|\rceil + \lceil\log_2 |\alpha|\rceil.
\]
This bound is achieved by the protocol in which Bob sends his input $y$ to Alice,
and Alice computes and sends back the output $f(x, y)$.
